stem.text: Consider \( \lim_{x \to 2} \frac{x + 7}{x - 2} \). Classify the form of this limit, name the procedure that resolves it, and give the result.

answer_key.label: Substitution gives \( \frac{9}{0} \), so check the sign on each side of \( x = 2 \), which gives \( -\infty \) and \( \infty \), so no limit exists.

worked_solution.text: Substituting \( x = 2 \) gives \( \frac{9}{0} \), a nonzero number over 0. This is not an indeterminate form, and the quotient is unbounded near \( x = 2 \).
The numerator is near 9. The denominator \( x - 2 \) is positive on the right of 2 and negative on the left, so the quotient approaches \( -\infty \) from the left and \( \infty \) from the right.
The two sides disagree, so the limit does not exist.

options.label: The quotient is undefined at \( x = 2 \), and no limit of any kind exists where a quotient is undefined, which means no sign check is needed.
options.derivation: nonexistence concluded because the expression is undefined at the point, with no sign check

options.label: Substitution gives \( \frac{9}{0} \), so check the sign on each side of \( x = 2 \), which gives \( -\infty \) and \( \infty \), so no limit exists.
The denominator \( x - 2 \) has a limit, so divide the limit of the numerator by it, which gives \( \frac{9}{0} \).
options.derivation: the quotient limit theorem chosen although the denominator's limit is 0

options.label: Substitution gives \( \frac{9}{0} \), so the quotient grows without bound, which gives \( \infty \) from both sides.
options.derivation: one two sided infinite limit written without checking the sign on each side
